subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: The Value of Redundancy
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Value of Redundancy usable.

hook.text: Ariane 5 had two computers running identical code. Both crashed at the same moment. Redundancy needs diversity.

buildup.text: Redundancy means having backup systems that take over when the primary fails—a core safety principle.

discovery.text: But identical backups fail identically. True redundancy requires different implementations or diverse approaches.

twist.text: N-version programming—building the same system multiple ways—is expensive. Most teams can't afford it.

climax.text: Practical redundancy combines diverse monitoring, graceful degradation, and automatic failover to limit damage.

punchline.text: A backup that fails the same way isn't a backup.

quiz.question: Why did Ariane 5's redundancy fail?
options: Both computers ran identical code and crashed identically
